title: Cross-border transfer
brief: 17:05. Two requests to share data land in your queue. One is routine. The other is an international transfer, dressed up as a support ticket.
role: Accounts payable, clearing the data sharing queue tonight
insight: A transfer is not only an upload to a foreign server. Letting people in another country read the data counts too.
teaches: Spot the transfer: data read from outside the UK is a transfer, even inside a support ticket
Know when it is fine (an adequate country) and when it needs safeguards (clauses and a risk assessment)
Send only what the job needs, and nothing until the safeguards are in place

value.title: Dublin office: vendor contact list
body: “Could you share the AP vendor contact list (names, work emails and phone numbers) with our Dublin office? We are taking over the Irish suppliers next month.”

sections.title: Does this need extra transfer safeguards?

options.label: No: Ireland is in the EEA, which UK law treats as adequate
options.why: Data can flow to the EEA without extra safeguards. It still goes through a Veltrix only link.

options.label: Yes, block it until a transfer assessment is done
options.why: Not needed for the EEA. Blocking it only holds up the handover.

value.title: Support ticket 7724: overnight desk access
body: “Hi AP team, BluePier, our new overnight support partner, needs read access to the full customer delivery file so their agents in their Cebu office can answer tracking calls from tonight.”
“Can you share the whole folder with support@bluepier-desk.net? Customers are waiting. Thanks!”
The folder holds 38,412 customers' names, home addresses, phone numbers and delivery notes.

policy.title: Veltrix international transfers
lines: Personal data going to, or read from, a country outside the UK needs an adequacy decision for that country, or signed transfer clauses (IDTA or the Addendum) plus a transfer risk assessment.
Share only what the recipient needs. The DPO approves every new transfer.

options.label: Yes: customer data would be read from outside the UK
options.why: Access from Cebu is a transfer, even though nothing is emailed.

options.label: No, it is only a support ticket
options.why: The ticket is the wrapper. Inside it is 38,412 people's data going abroad.

sections.title: 2. What has to be in place first?

options.label: Signed international transfer clauses, as there is no UK adequacy decision for that country
options.why: The legal route for a country without adequacy.

options.label: A transfer risk assessment
options.why: It checks the clauses will actually protect people there.

options.label: Only the fields agents need to answer tracking calls, not the whole file
options.why: Tracking needs an order number and a status, not home addresses and phone numbers.

options.label: BluePier's assurance that they are secure
options.why: Assurances are not a legal basis for a transfer.

options.label: Hold: share nothing until the DPO confirms the safeguards
options.why: Customers wait one more night. Their data does not leave without protection.

options.label: Share the whole folder now, customers are waiting
options.why: An unlawful transfer of the whole customer file, to meet a queue.

choices.label: Two sharing requests: our Dublin office, and an offshore support desk

script.say: Dublin is fine, the EEA counts as adequate. The offshore desk is a restricted transfer: I need signed clauses and a risk assessment first, and they only get the fields they need. Nothing tonight.

setup.title: Work queue
setup.body: Two data sharing requests are waiting

outcome.label: Asked data protection
outcome.what: Dublin is fine; the offshore desk needs clauses, an assessment and minimisation.
outcome.ideal: checks new transfers with the DPO.

outcome.label: Spotted the transfer inside the ticket
outcome.what: Read access from another country is a transfer, however the request is worded.
outcome.ideal: recognises a transfer hidden in an ordinary request.

outcome.label: Let the routine transfer through
outcome.what: Ireland is in the EEA: no extra safeguards needed.
outcome.ideal: knows when a transfer is fine, not only when it is not.

outcome.label: Blocked a transfer that was fine
outcome.what: Data can flow to the EEA. Blocking it held up a real handover.
outcome.ideal: saves the safeguards for the transfers that need them.

decide.objective: Clear the data sharing queue: one is routine, one is not.
decide.insight: Where is the data going, or being read from? That one question finds the transfer.

hint.text: Open the Work queue. Let the Dublin request through. For ticket 7724: it is a transfer, it needs clauses, a risk assessment and minimisation, and you hold it tonight. Data protection is on 4120.

outcome.label: Held the offshore transfer until it is safe
outcome.what: Nothing leaves tonight. BluePier gets only the tracking fields, once the clauses and assessment are signed off.
outcome.ideal: spots a transfer and holds it until the safeguards are in place.

card.title: The transfer in the ticket
body: It looked like a support ticket. It was a request to open 38,412 customers' data to a desk in another country with no adequacy decision.
You held it, required the clauses and a risk assessment, and cut it down to what the agents actually need. Dublin, in the EEA, went straight through.
card.ideal: asks where the data goes, and applies the safeguards that fit.

outcome.label: Shared the whole customer file offshore
outcome.what: The full customer file is now readable from another country with no legal safeguards in place.
outcome.ideal: holds a restricted transfer until the safeguards are signed.

card.title: Across the border, unprotected
body: Sharing the folder was an international transfer with no clauses, no assessment, and far more data than tracking calls need.
“Customers are waiting” is the pressure that hides the transfer. One night's wait was the right answer.
card.ideal: spots the transfer, minimises, and waits for safeguards.

outcome.label: Missed part of the transfer check
outcome.what: The transfer was held or answered with a gap: a missing safeguard, or trust in the supplier's word.
outcome.ideal: requires clauses, a risk assessment and minimisation.

card.title: Nearly
body: Something was missing from the safeguards. Open the case to see which answer was off.
card.ideal: knows the three things a restricted transfer needs.
